name: Delney, Streetwise Lookout doubles Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy's own triggered mana ability -> +2 mana per qualifying nonland mana activation

prerequisites.timing: Any time a nonland permanent you control is tapped for mana (most commonly during a main phase while developing mana dorks/rocks). No sorcery-speed restriction applies to either card's relevant ability.
other: Kinnan's power is exactly 2, so its own triggered ability ('Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced.') qualifies for Delney's power-2-or-less doubling clause - no third card is required.

Delney's own official ruling (2024-02-02, Scryfall-sourced): 'Delney, Streetwise Lookout's last ability doesn't copy the triggered ability; it just causes the ability to trigger an additional time. Any choices made as you put the ability onto the stack, such as modes and targets, are made separately for each instance of the ability.' This directly confirms the doubling applies generically to any qualifying triggered ability, including Kinnan's own.

IMPORTANT correction (2026-08-12, caught by user review of the initial writeup): Kinnan's ability text is 'add ONE mana of any type that permanent produced' - a FLAT one mana per trigger instance, not a copy or multiplier of the tapped permanent's own output. The correct general model is: total mana = (mana the tapped nonland permanent itself produces) + 2 (one from Kinnan's own trigger, one from the Delney-granted additional instance of that same trigger). This is NOT 'triple mana from any nonland source' - that abstraction is only true by coincidence for exactly-1-mana sources. For a 1-mana source (Devoted Druid, Birds of Paradise, Mox Diamond, etc.): 1 + 2 = 3 (happens to triple). For Sol Ring (2 mana): 2 + 2 = 4 (not 6). For Mana Vault (3 mana): 3 + 2 = 5 (not 9). See rules_tests/gold_board_states/GBS-0002.json (1-mana case) and GBS-0003.json (2-mana Sol Ring case, added specifically to engine-verify the +2 model against the erroneous multiplier abstraction) for both engine-reproduced data points.
Does not apply to lands (Kinnan's trigger condition explicitly excludes them), so it does not touch Gaea's Cradle or basic/nonbasic lands directly.

Not a loop and not infinite by itself - a static per-tap bonus of +2 mana, bounded by however many nonland mana sources are tapped that turn. Could compose with other mana lines but does not itself produce unbounded mana.

result.summary: Every tap of a nonland permanent you control for mana produces 2 additional mana (one from Kinnan's own triggered mana ability, one from the extra instance of that trigger granted by Delney), on top of whatever that permanent already produces, as long as both Delney and Kinnan are on the battlefield. This is a flat +2 bonus per activation, not a multiplier of the source's own output.

rules_citations: CR 603.2d — an ability may state that a triggered ability triggers additional times; in this case, rather than simply determining that such an ability has triggered, determine how many times it should trigger, then that ability triggers that many times. This is the mechanic Delney's static ability relies on, and it applies generically to any qualifying triggered ability, including one that is itself a mana-related trigger.

CR 605.1b — a triggered ability is a mana ability if it doesn't require a target, it triggers from the activation or resolution of an activated mana ability (or from mana being added to a player's mana pool), and it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves. Kinnan's 'Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced' meets all three criteria (no target, triggers from activating a mana ability, adds mana on resolution) and is therefore itself a triggered mana ability.

CR 605.4 / 605.4a — triggered mana abilities follow all the rules for other triggered abilities (including 603.2d, so Delney's doubling still applies), but do not go on the stack and resolve immediately after the mana ability that triggered them, without waiting for priority. This is why both instances of Kinnan's doubled trigger resolve immediately alongside the initial tap, rather than requiring separate stack resolution.

executable_engine_check.notes: Reproduced in the same from-source Maven build of magefree/mage (JDK 21, Mage/Mage.Sets/Mage.Tests modules) used for INT-0002, via two JUnit tests (neither committed to this repo — XMage is separately-licensed engine source, cloned to scratch space; see docs/RUN_CLASSIFICATION.md, rules_tests/gold_board_states/GBS-0002.json, and rules_tests/gold_board_states/GBS-0003.json for the fixture records and provenance). Test 1 (1-mana source): org.mage.test.cards.interactions.cedh.DelneyKinnanTripleManaTest#test_DelneyDoublesKinnansOwnTrigger_TripleManaFromOneTap - Delney + Kinnan + Devoted Druid (an arbitrary nonland 1-mana source; its identity is not material to this interaction), activated Devoted Druid's {T}: Add {G} once, result 3 total {G} in the mana pool (1 + 2). Passed 1/1 on first attempt. Test 2 (2-mana source, added specifically to rule out an over-generalized 'triples everything' misreading of test 1's coincidental result): org.mage.test.cards.interactions.cedh.DelneyKinnanSolRingPlusTwoTest#test_DelneyKinnan_SolRing_IsPlusTwoNotTripled - Delney + Kinnan + Sol Ring, activated Sol Ring's {T}: Add {C}{C} once, result 4 total {C} in the mana pool (2 + 2, NOT 6 which a flat tripling model would incorrectly predict). Passed 1/1 on first attempt. Both engine results match the CR 605.1b/605.4a analysis: each trigger instance adds exactly one mana regardless of the tapped permanent's own output.
